keyVerseText: So they went up, and searched the land from the wilderness of Zin unto Rehob, as men come to Hamath.
rootMeaning: The root of רְחֹב (Rᵉchôb) conveys the idea of a 'broad place' or 'broad way,' emphasizing spaciousness and openness. This literal sense of width or an open area goes beyond the common English gloss of a mere place name, suggesting a location characterized by expansiveness or a wide avenue. The root word רְחֹב (rᵉchôb) itself also means a broad or open plaza, highlighting a physical dimension of breadth that may symbolize accessibility or prominence within the landscape.
usageInScripture: The term רְחֹב appears ten times in Scripture with consistent translations related to the place name Rehob, often rendered simply as 'Rehob' or with prepositions such as 'and Rehob' or 'of Rehob.' Its usage spans references to locations in Syria and towns in the tribe of Asher, as well as personal names, including a Levite and a Syrian figure. This range shows that while the word primarily identifies geographic places, it also functions as a personal name, maintaining the core idea of a broad or significant place within different contexts.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding רְחֹב as a 'broad place' enriches our grasp of biblical geography and the spiritual symbolism of space in Scripture. The expansiveness implied by the word can remind believers of God's provision of wide-open places for His people—spaces of refuge, covenant, and mission. The fact that Rehob marks a boundary in the exploration of the Promised Land underscores God's sovereignty over the land and His guidance in the journey of faith. This broad place thus becomes a metaphor for the spiritual openness God offers through Christ, inviting His people to walk in the fullness of His promises.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 13:21 states, 'So they went up, and searched the land from the wilderness of Zin unto Rehob, as men come to Hamath.' Here, רְחֹב (Rehob) defines the northern boundary of the spies' exploration of Canaan, emphasizing the extent and thoroughness of their survey. The word's meaning as a broad place highlights the vastness of the land God was giving to Israel, reinforcing the faith required to claim such a spacious inheritance. It also points to God's faithfulness in providing a wide and open territory for His people to inhabit.
